hypothesis: Time-scaling the same joint paths reduces release-time motion and improves full-program task outcomes
invariants: All 18 joint-position arrays identical to source
Joint names and gripper/atom event order unchanged
No initial teleport, same strict continuity checks
Source manifest and NPZ files untouched
No target, geometry, friction or tolerance changes
conclusion: Slower commanded trajectories do not monotonically improve held-object motion or task success. Do not enable a default time scale or relax tolerances based on these trials.
raw_log_rule: Each raw_dir has a matching adjacent .log file
limitations: Retimed diagnostic, not unmodified portable-program replay
Only one frozen synthetic distribution, not measured U1 suite
Timing change also changes elapsed settling/contact dynamics; does not isolate a unique cause
No complete SIM safety gate or physical trial approval
